title: narcissus tazetta subsp. canariensis
intro: Narcissus tazetta subsp. canariensis, commonly known as the Canary Islands Daffodil, is a subspecies of flowering plant that belongs to the genus Narcissus and is native to the Canary Islands. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can help to boost the immune system, reduce stress and anxiety, and protect against cell damage. The therapeutic actions of Narcissus tazetta subsp. canariensis include its ability to act as a sedative, antispasmodic, and anti-inflammatory agent, making it useful in the treatment of digestive issues, insomnia, and skin conditions. The plant contains bioactive constituents such as alkaloids, flavonoids, and saponins, which are responsible for its therapeutic properties and have been shown to exhibit potential anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory activities.
